propositions: Plan asserts that a named module or symbol provides a capability that it does not actually provide, causing the agent to build on non-existent functionality (capability-present-in-plan-but-absent-in-code)
Plan asserts that a capability is absent or must be built, but the named module already provides it, causing unnecessary duplication or redundant work (capability-absent-in-plan-but-present-in-code)
The new asserted-capability criterion ships as advisory and non-blocking, with registration in CANONICAL_LLM, CODEBASE_GROUNDED, and AGENT_TIER registries plus routing entry in criteria_routing.json
The criterion is grounded by code inspection via resolve_symbol and grepping the repository to verify actual module capability surfaces against plan assertions

Deterministic unit tests validate registration invariants, routing shape, and prompt-contract sub-answer keys; a bounded sanity check on 3 E1-verified misses (dc58, db7b, 5886) and 3 clean controls confirms >=66% recall threshold
The criterion auto-flows into the standing effectiveness recorder with zero per-criterion wiring and is subject to an advisory-to-blocking promotion gate gated on future dogfood accumulation
